body.x: Calmantech (CEO Jaehwan Choi) participated in the “Global Media Online Meetup” held on July 2 with Ubergizmo, a U.S.-based tech media outlet, targeting Korean startups and companies.

Jointly hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, the meetup aimed to introduce Korean companies and technologies to global audiences, particularly highlighting CES 2026 Innovation Award candidates and startups preparing to exhibit.

Founded in 2021, Calmantech is developing a next-generation mobility paradigm with omnidirectional autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that move freely in all directions. The company’s goal is to help manufacturers and service providers adopt AMRs even in narrow and complex environments.

Calmantech previously implemented its AMR solution at the component manufacturing plant of Sambo A&T, a Tier-1 Hyundai Motor supplier. Despite the plant’s tight and overlapping pathways, the system successfully enabled stable and efficient logistics automation.

The company continues to receive inquiries from mid-sized manufacturers with similar layouts. It is expanding into service sectors such as hotels and hospitals, where it is currently conducting PoC (proof of concept) trials.

body.cap: AMR product image | Image provided by Calmantech

body.x: At CES 2026, Calmantech will unveil its AMR equipped with four ball-wheel mechanisms that enable movement across X, Y, and θ axes. The robot features proprietary ROS2-based autonomous driving software supporting real-time SLAM, obstacle avoidance, path recalculation, and unstructured docking.

The robot’s standout features include precise and fast direction changes without steering, enabling high-precision autonomous driving in tight, intricate spaces. Compared to mecanum or omni-wheel systems, Calmantech’s ball-wheel system provides higher power efficiency, minimal turning radius, and improved mechanical durability with simple drive structures.
The robot fuses 2D LiDAR and RGB camera data to generate high-precision 3D maps, supporting autonomous navigation with a docking accuracy of ±2mm.

body.cap: AMR product image | Image provided by Calmantech

body.x: Calmantech’s AMR also excels in aesthetic and functional design. Inspired by the “Hover Stream” concept, it features smooth curves and dynamic directional lighting. The modular upper structure allows easy customization for diverse use cases.

Another key innovation is Calmantech’s proprietary ball-wheel mechanism, which addresses the power loss, friction, vibration, and floor damage issues seen in existing omnidirectional drive systems. It also overcomes the mechanical complexity and slow response times of swivel wheels.

Combined with ROS2-based autonomy, the system integrates deep learning-powered pedestrian recognition and collision avoidance, enabling precise navigation and docking in human-populated, complex environments.

body.cap: Calmantech’s Global Media Meetup team with Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen (center) and CEO Jaehwan Choi (right) | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Calmantech aims to expand globally, starting with the EU and U.S. markets. In Europe, the company is preparing to deploy its AMRs at Plakor’s Czech plant, a subsidiary of Sambo Motors Group. The robots are currently undergoing CE certification.

In the U.S., where small and mid-sized factories lack smart factory infrastructure, Calmantech sees strong demand for compact AMRs. The company seeks logistics automation partners through CES 2026 and anticipates collaborations with local consulting firms and Tier 1 suppliers in the battery and automotive industries.

PoC trials are also being prepared in Singapore for Southeast Asia expansion. Efforts include the development of multilingual robot operation software and upgrades to the remote robot control system. Calmantech is also working on expanding its modular AMR lineup, enhancing its lightweight ROS2-based AI autonomy software, and commercializing high-resolution 3D SLAM technologies.
A Calmantech official stated, “Based on our proven performance in Korea, we aim to offer practical, space-efficient solutions for industries worldwide facing similar logistical challenges.”

body.x: Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
